# Problem

Instructors need to judge a tutorial's content, prerequisites, difficulty, and duration, but course sites and package documentation describe these inconsistently. A tutorial may remain online after its exercises stop working or its author stops maintaining it.

learnr runs tutorials as Shiny applications [@learnr]. learnr2 builds on Quarto Live, which uses webR to execute R in the browser [@learnr2; @quartolive]. tutorialverse will connect these authoring approaches through common tutorial descriptions, validation records, and discovery. Carpentries and Bioconductor materials will provide additional teaching contexts.

## Evidence of need and prior work

Educators have long had to compare overlapping tools. @handel2025 assessed learnr, webexercises, checkdown, exams, quarto-webr, and quarto-live against his requirements for hosting, maintenance, and exercise types. [Kranz's 2019 comparison](https://skranz.github.io/r/2019/04/29/RTutor_vs_Learnr.html) of RTutor and learnr shows that choices about exercise structure, teaching environments, and long-term support predate webR.

Discussions in the learnr community document difficulties [integrating custom Shiny questions](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/discussions/719) and a report of [Python exercises working locally but failing after deployment](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/821). These reports illustrate support needs; they do not establish how often tutorials fail.

The [rstats-ed project](https://github.com/rstudio-education/rstats-ed) assembled a user-curated discovery list of R courses and learning materials, acknowledging that it could not be comprehensive. TeSS aggregates training metadata, and Bioschemas provides shared descriptions for training resources [@garcia2020; @castro2023]. Glittr.org helps users find and compare teaching repositories; its 2024 paper explicitly excludes evaluation of their educational quality [@vangeest2024].

The Galaxy Training Network provides a precedent for combining automated checks with community review and ongoing maintenance [@hiltemann2023].

tutorialverse will build on these approaches, mapping tutorial descriptions to existing standards and recording which exercises and dependencies were checked, in which environment, and when. Its registry will combine these records with review and maintenance information. Existing engines will run the tutorials; the project will not build a new engine, browser runtime, or learning-management system. Static hosting will remain a deployment mode to describe and check.
